Pancho Villa. Born Doroteo Arango. The northern Mexican revolutionary general whose Division del Norte became the largest military force during the Mexican Revolution. Known for dramatic cavalry charges and agrarian zeal, he commanded peasant armies while resisting foreign intervention.

Villa rose from banditry to command the Division del Norte, the revolution's most formidable military force, with over fifty thousand soldiers under his command. He allied with Emiliano Zapata in the south to challenge both the Porfiriato and later centrist revolutionary governments. He became legendary for his lightning cavalry raids and bold military tactics throughout northern Mexico. In 1914 and 1915, he briefly held Mexico City alongside Zapata before being defeated by the constitutionalist Venustiano Carranza. In 1916, Villa did something extraordinary. He crossed the United States border and attacked Columbus, New Mexico—the only foreign military force to invade the continental United States in a century. The raid shocked the nation and brought American military retaliation. Villa was assassinated in 1923 in Parral, Chihuahua. His legend grew immensely after his death, and he became remembered as a champion of the common man, standing alongside Zapata as one of the revolution's most iconic figures.
